note: Egyptian gods pack. Years BC are negative, following Shaw (ed.), Oxford History of Ancient Egypt (2000). 'from' is an approximate first attestation or rise to prominence, not a founding date; dates for gods are rough and can be pushed earlier by new finds. Alternative chronologies differ by decades in the Old Kingdom.

things.name: Amun
things.who: first attested in the Pyramid Texts; the national god of Egypt from the New Kingdom

things.name: Min (and Amun-Min-Kamutef)
things.who: an ancient fertility god of Koptos and Akhmim, merged with Amun as Amun-Min-Kamutef; earliest colossi are Predynastic

things.name: Mut
things.who: the vulture goddess and wife of Amun; important from the New Kingdom, though attested earlier

things.name: the Theban triad
things.who: the divine family of Amun, Mut and Khonsu; approximate start of the New Kingdom grouping

things.name: the god Khonsu
things.who: the moon god, son of Amun and Mut; first attested in the Pyramid Texts

things.name: Montu
things.who: the falcon war god of the Theban region; patron of the Eleventh Dynasty kings

things.name: Ptah
things.who: the creator and craftsmen's god of Memphis; worshipped from the Early Dynastic period

things.name: Sekhmet
things.who: the lioness goddess of war, plague and healing; attested in the Pyramid Texts

things.name: Hathor
things.who: the goddess of joy, music and motherhood; well attested by the Old Kingdom

things.name: the Eye of Ra story
things.who: the tale of the sun god's Eye turned into the lioness Sekhmet; known from royal tombs including Tutankhamun's (about 1323 BC)

things.name: Ra
things.who: the sun god, whose cult at Heliopolis made kings 'sons of Ra' from the Fourth Dynasty

things.name: the sun god's daily journey
things.who: the belief that Ra sails the sky by day and the underworld by night

things.name: Khepri
things.who: the scarab-beetle form of the rising sun

things.name: Horus
things.who: the falcon sky god embodied by every living king

things.name: Osiris
things.who: the god of the dead and resurrection; first firmly attested late in the Fifth Dynasty

things.name: Isis
things.who: the wife of Osiris, mother of Horus and mistress of magic

things.name: the Osiris myth
things.who: the story of the murdered king Osiris, Isis and Horus's revenge; alluded to in the Pyramid Texts, told in full by Plutarch about AD 100

things.name: the Aten
things.who: the sun disc, made the sole god by Akhenaten from about 1348 BC

things.name: sacred animals and animal-headed gods
things.who: the Egyptian habit of showing gods as animals or part-animals

things.name: Thoth
things.who: the ibis or baboon god of writing, wisdom and the moon

things.name: Anubis
things.who: the jackal god of embalming and cemeteries; may be older

things.name: Wadjet and Nekhbet
things.who: the cobra goddess of Lower Egypt and vulture goddess of Upper Egypt, protectors of the king

things.name: the sacred animal cults
things.who: the keeping and burying of sacred animals such as the Apis bull; mass animal mummy offerings belong to the Late and Ptolemaic periods

things.name: Maat
things.who: the goddess and principle of truth, order and justice, against chaos (isfet)

things.name: the king's duty to uphold Maat
things.who: the idea that the king kept the world in order by offering to the gods and defeating chaos

things.name: how Egyptian gods are shown
things.who: the visual code of crowns, animal heads and symbols used to name gods in art
